summary: Tether 0.30.3 gives every project a start page, and + opens it.

highlights.title: A start page for every project.
highlights.body: A project with no tabs open shows its icon, big Start Claude and Start Codex buttons, Shell, Agent on a Branch, its dev server preview and shortcuts, and your last few conversations to pick back up in a click. A newly added project opens on it, so you choose Claude or Codex.

highlights.title: + opens the start page.
highlights.body: Instead of a small menu, + shows the start page in place of the current tab. Pick anything, click another tab or press Esc to close it. ⌘T still opens Claude right away, and ⌥⌘T Codex.

summary: Tether 0.30.2 puts Codex next to Claude everywhere you start a tab, including on a paired Mac and the iPhone.

highlights.title: Codex, wherever Claude is.
highlights.body: A Codex button sits next to Claude in the tab bar. Agent on a Branch, the Overview and New Task on the iPhone let you choose Claude or Codex.

highlights.title: Codex on your other Mac.
highlights.body: With a paired Mac in view, the Codex button, the + menu and File > New Codex Tab open the tab on that Mac. File > New Claude Tab does the same now, instead of opening it on this Mac out of sight. Both Macs and the iPhone need this version.

summary: Tether 0.30.1 offers Claude's suggested next message in the chat view.

highlights.title: Claude's suggestion, in the chat.
highlights.body: When Claude finishes and suggests what to say next, the suggestion shows faintly in the empty message box. Press Tab or Right Arrow to take it, edit it if you like, then Return to send.

summary: Tether 0.30.0 puts Codex beside Claude: Codex tabs with live status, approvals from the Mac or iPhone, and Stop.

highlights.title: Codex tabs.
highlights.body: Choose Codex from a project's + menu, or File > New Codex Tab (Option-Command-T). Tether runs OpenAI's Codex CLI in the project's folder, and reopens it on the same thread next launch. The first time, Codex asks you to review Tether's hooks: choose Trust all and continue. Codex remembers that.

highlights.title: Same status, same approvals.
highlights.body: A Codex tab's badge shows working, done and needs-you like a Claude tab, in the sidebar, the Overview, the menu bar and on the iPhone. When Codex asks to run something, the card says Codex wants to, and you can allow or deny it from the Mac, the iPhone or the lock screen.

highlights.title: Messages and Stop from the iPhone.
highlights.body: Messages you send a Codex tab wait until it finishes its turn, like Claude's. Stop works too. Codex's replies stay in its terminal for now; the chat view for Codex comes next.

highlights.title: Update everything together.
highlights.body: Update Tether on every Mac and the iPhone: older copies can't talk to this one.

summary: Tether 0.20.13 shows Claude's subagents and background commands in the chat view.

highlights.title: See Claude's subagents.
highlights.body: When Claude sends out agents, each gets a card in the chat with what it's for, a spinner while it works, and how it ended. While any are running, a line above the message box lists them, so they don't scroll away.

highlights.title: Background work says when it's done.
highlights.body: When a background agent or command finishes, a quiet line in the chat says so, with the command's exit code. The step that started it updates at the same moment, on the Mac and the iPhone.

summary: Tether 0.20.12 makes the project list sort itself: Active projects by recent use, Pin to Top, and a folding Inactive section, on the Mac and iPhone.

highlights.title: Active projects take care of themselves.
highlights.body: Projects you've worked in lately show under Active, most recent first. Sending Claude a prompt, opening a tab, Claude starting a turn, and Claude Code used outside Tether all count. After 3 days without use (change it in Settings > Appearance) a project folds into Inactive, and it comes back as soon as you use it.

highlights.title: Pin to Top.
highlights.body: Right-click a project and choose Pin to Top to keep it at the top of Active. Drag pinned projects to put them in your order. Move to Inactive and Make Active are in the same menu.

highlights.title: The iPhone and your other Macs match.
highlights.body: The iPhone shows the same Active list with a folding Inactive section; long-press a project to pin it or move it. A paired Mac's sidebar does the same. Update Tether on every Mac and the iPhone together.

summary: Tether 0.20.11 makes the chat's message box do more: change queued messages, send one right away, and keep your draft per tab.

highlights.title: Edit, remove or send queued messages now.
highlights.body: A message you sent while Claude was busy has Edit, Remove and Send Now under it. Send Now stops the step Claude is on and sends that message by itself; the others stay queued. Control-Return in the message box does the same for what you've typed.

highlights.title: Your draft stays with its tab.
highlights.body: Text and pictures in the message box stay with the tab you typed them in, through switching tabs, projects, or to the terminal and back.

highlights.title: Compact, clear and attach without typing.
highlights.body: The new / button runs Compact Conversation or Clear Conversation, and the paperclip attaches pictures from disk. Shift-Return or Option-Return starts a new line.

highlights.title: Copy a message, and right-click changed files.
highlights.body: Hover over a message for a copy button. Files in the Changes list now open, show in Finder, or copy their full or relative path from the right-click menu.

highlights.title: A quieter context meter, and Fable.
highlights.body: The context meter stays grey until 70%, then turns orange, and red from 85%. The model menu offers Fable.

summary: Tether 0.20.10 lets you read back through a paired Mac's chat without being pulled to the bottom.

highlights.title: A paired Mac's chat stays where you scrolled.
highlights.body: In Remote Macs, the chat follows Claude only while you're at the end. Scroll up and it stays put, with a Jump to latest button to get back. Sending a message also brings you to the end, the same as a chat on this Mac.

summary: Tether 0.20.9 stops running Claude tabs from showing as Ended on your iPhone.

highlights.title: Live tabs no longer show as Ended.
highlights.body: A late end-of-session message from a tab's previous session could mark a running tab as Ended, which left it read-only on the iPhone until Claude did something. Tether now ignores those, and a tab whose Claude is visibly running is treated as live again.

summary: Tether 0.20.8 fixes Trust Folder, which quit Claude instead of trusting the folder.

highlights.title: Trust Folder trusts the folder.
highlights.body: Claude's trust question now lists "No, exit" first, so the Trust button on the Mac and iPhone picked No and Claude quit. It now picks "Yes, I trust this folder".

summary: Tether 0.20.7 refines the iPhone's new look: better contrast, nicer questions, and every sheet in your colors.

highlights.title: Questions you can tap.
highlights.body: When Claude asks a question, the iPhone shows each option as a numbered card, matching the numbers in the terminal, with a field for an answer of your own.

highlights.title: Easier to read.
highlights.body: Secondary text on the iPhone has more contrast, nothing is clipped at the edges anymore, and the standard iOS look no longer draws dark lines between tabs.

highlights.title: Every screen matches.
highlights.body: New Task, Edit Projects, Changes and Pair a Mac now follow your Mac's colors like the rest of the iPhone app. This needs the new iPhone build.

summary: Tether 0.20.5 makes it clear when a new Claude tab is waiting on the terminal.

highlights.title: Chat tells you when Claude hasn't started.
highlights.body: In a folder Claude hasn't opened before, it asks whether to trust the files before it starts, and messages you send wait until then. The chat now says when Claude hasn't started yet, with a button to show the terminal, and Mode and Model stay disabled until Claude is running so they can't press keys into that question.

highlights.title: Fewer stray folder-trust alerts.
highlights.body: Your phone is alerted about the trust question only once it has waited a few seconds, and the alert clears as soon as Claude is running.

summary: Tether 0.20.4 gives the iPhone app a proper design, in your Mac's colors.

highlights.title: Answer from the overview.
highlights.body: Permissions and folder-trust prompts now show as cards with Allow and Deny right on them, at the top of the iPhone's overview and above the message box in a chat. Tap the card to see the whole request first. Questions open their options with Answer.

highlights.title: Claude tabs that show what they're doing.
highlights.body: Each tab shows the same sparkles, pulsing dot and check as the Mac's sidebar, with a tidy mode chip, and your Macs appear as chips with their connection status. Plan usage sits in one compact card.

highlights.title: A chat that feels like a chat.
highlights.body: The message box, Send button, your bubbles, tool steps and the permission sheet now follow your Mac's terminal colors like the rest of the app. This needs the new iPhone build.

summary: Tether 0.20.3 makes the chat easier to follow while Claude works.

highlights.title: The chat stays at the bottom.
highlights.body: New text and tool steps now follow along as the conversation grows. Scroll up to read something earlier and it stays put, with a button to jump back to the latest. Sending a message always brings you back down.

highlights.title: See messages you've queued.
highlights.body: A message you send while Claude is busy shows up right away as a Queued bubble at the end of the chat. It becomes a normal message once Claude reads it.

highlights.title: Paste images into the chat.
highlights.body: Press Command-V in the message box to attach a screenshot, a copied image, or image files copied in Finder. Text still pastes as text.

summary: Tether 0.20.2 opens long conversations in a moment.

highlights.title: Big chats open in a moment.
highlights.body: Long Claude sessions write transcripts of hundreds of megabytes, and the chat used to read all of it before showing anything. Now it reads from the end, just far enough to show the recent conversation. The top of the chat says when older messages are left out, and nothing in the transcript is changed. Your phone and other Macs get the same speedup.

summary: Tether 0.20.1 puts Stop, edits and your terminal's colors on the iPhone, and adds mode and model switching to the chat.

highlights.title: Stop from your phone or another Mac.
highlights.body: While Claude is working, the iPhone and a paired Mac's chat show a Stop button that stops the turn on the Mac. Commands you stopped or denied read "Stopped", not "Failed".

highlights.title: Edits and commands on the iPhone.
highlights.body: The phone now shows the file Claude touched, the lines an edit changed, and whether each command worked, with the last lines it printed. This needs the new iPhone build.

highlights.title: Your phone in your Mac's colors.
highlights.body: The iPhone app can take on the background and text colors of your Ghostty theme, light or dark. Turn it off from the phone's menu with Use Mac's Colors.

highlights.title: Mode and model from the chat.
highlights.body: The chat header has a mode menu and a model menu, so you can switch without going back to the terminal. The sidebar's update button now opens Settings > Updates.

summary: Tether 0.20.0 brings the chat view up to a full alternative to the terminal, and lets you answer Claude's questions from anywhere.

highlights.title: Chat or terminal, per tab.
highlights.body: Switch a Claude tab between its terminal and its chat with the buttons in the tab bar or View > Show as Chat (⇧⌘M). Settings > Appearance picks which one new Claude tabs open in. Claude keeps running in the terminal either way.

highlights.title: See what Claude did.
highlights.body: In the chat, files Claude read or edited open when you click them, edits show the lines that changed, and commands show whether they worked, were stopped or failed, with the last lines they printed.

highlights.title: Stop, and what Claude is doing.
highlights.body: Above the message box the chat shows what Claude is doing, how long the turn has run, and a Stop button. Permission cards sit right above the message box too: with it empty, Return allows and Esc denies.

highlights.title: Answer Claude's questions anywhere.
highlights.body: When Claude asks you to pick from options, they appear as a card on the Mac, the iPhone and a paired Mac, with a field for an answer of your own. Questions with several parts or multiple choices still go to the terminal.

highlights.title: Trust a new folder from your phone.
highlights.body: When Claude starts in a folder it hasn't opened before, it asks whether you trust it before doing anything else. That question now shows as a card you can answer from the Mac, your iPhone or another Mac. Tether only passes your answer along; it never trusts a folder for you. Rebuild the iPhone app to get the new cards.

summary: Tether 0.10.9 shows plan usage in the chat.

highlights.title: 5-hour and 7-day plan usage.
highlights.body: Two small bars beside the context meter show how much of your plan's 5-hour and weekly limits are used, on this Mac and on a paired Mac. They appear once Claude Code has reported them; hover for the reset time.

summary: Tether 0.10.8 adds Files and Preview for a paired Mac.

highlights.title: Files and Preview on another Mac.
highlights.body: The right sidebar for a paired Mac now has Changes, Files and Preview, like this Mac's. Files browses the tab's folder there; Preview opens a dev server running there, as long as it listens beyond localhost (for example, started with --host). Update both Macs.

highlights.title: Context and cost on a paired Mac's chat.
highlights.body: The chat strip shows the tab's state, model, cost and how much context it has used, like the origin Mac.

summary: Tether 0.10.7 tucks Mac connection problems out of the way.

highlights.title: A quieter notice for another Mac.
highlights.body: When a paired Mac needs an update or can't be reached, a small card at the bottom of the sidebar says why, instead of text above its projects. Close it with the x.

highlights.title: No terminal button on another Mac.
highlights.body: A paired Mac's tabs are chat only, so the greyed-out terminal toggle is gone.

summary: Tether 0.10.6 adds History and Changes for a paired Mac.

highlights.title: History and Changes on another Mac.
highlights.body: With a paired Mac selected, History lists that project's past sessions and reopens one in a tab there, and the right sidebar button shows the tab's changes and diffs. Update both Macs: the Macs now speak a newer version. Terminals still stay on the other Mac.

highlights.title: A new tab on another Mac shows its conversation.
highlights.body: Fixes a new tab that could stay on Nothing yet after you sent a message.

summary: Tether 0.10.5 makes another Mac look like this one.

highlights.title: Same layout on a paired Mac.
highlights.body: A paired Mac's project now has the same tab strip and buttons as a local one: its Claude tabs, the chat view, Claude, + and the sidebar toggle. Terminals and History stay on the other Mac for now.

highlights.title: The + chip opens Settings → Macs.
highlights.body: Clicking + beside the Mac chips now lands on the Macs tab instead of whichever tab you used last.

summary: Tether 0.10.4 lets you start Claude tabs on a paired Mac.

highlights.title: New tab on another Mac.
highlights.body: With a paired Mac selected in the sidebar, click + beside its projects, or right-click a project and choose New Claude Tab…. Pick the project, optionally a new branch (the other Mac makes the worktree), say what Claude should do, and the tab opens here.

summary: Tether 0.10.3 shows a paired Mac's projects in the sidebar.

highlights.title: Other Macs in the sidebar.
highlights.body: The sidebar has a chip for This Mac and one for each paired Mac. Pick a paired Mac to see its projects and Claude tabs, read the conversation, answer permission prompts and send messages. The + chip opens Settings → Macs.

highlights.title: Pairing lives in Settings → Macs.
highlights.body: Copy Pairing Link on the Mac you want to follow, then Paste and Pair on the other one. Settings → iPhone is now only for the phone.

summary: Tether 0.10.2 makes pairing another Mac one step with a clear pass or fail.

highlights.title: Settings → Macs.
highlights.body: Pairing another Mac now lives in Settings → Macs: click Paste and Pair after copying the link from the other Mac's Settings → iPhone. Tether connects right away and says whether it worked, and each paired Mac shows whether it's reachable, with a Test button. The old Remote Hosts tab is now called SSH Hosts.

summary: Tether 0.10.1 fixes the version number and simplifies Settings → Updates.

highlights.title: Updates settings.
highlights.body: Settings → Updates now shows the real version, and the GitHub token field is gone: Tether reads the public releases page without signing in.

summary: Tether 0.10.0 lets one Mac follow and answer the Claude tabs on another.

highlights.title: Remote Macs.
highlights.body: Pair a second Mac the way you pair an iPhone: on the Mac running Claude, open Settings → iPhone, click Pair iPhone or Mac…, then Copy Link. On the other Mac, open Window → Remote Macs and paste it. You can read each tab's conversation, allow or deny permissions, and send messages. Both Macs need Tailscale.

summary: Tether 0.9.0 adds a Preview panel that shows your dev server next to the terminal.

highlights.title: Preview.
highlights.body: The inspector has a third tab, Preview (Shift-Command-P). It finds the dev server running in the selected project or branch by its port and shows it in a browser, with no setup. Pick another server from the network menu, type an address or port, or open the page in your browser.

summary: Tether 0.8.0 lets the iPhone app show a tab's changes and send Claude a photo. Update both the Mac and iPhone apps.

highlights.title: Changes on iPhone.
highlights.body: In a session on your iPhone, the ··· menu has Changes: the same files and line counts as the Mac's Changes panel. Tap a file to read its diff.

highlights.title: Photos for Claude.
highlights.body: The photo button next to the iPhone's message box attaches a picture, with an optional note. The Mac saves it and tells Claude where it is, so you can send a screenshot of a bug or a sketch of a layout.

summary: Tether 0.7.0 lets you stage and unstage files from the Changes panel, and shows how long each turn has been running.

highlights.title: Staging.
highlights.body: Each file with uncommitted changes in Changes shows an empty circle, a half circle or a check for unstaged, partly staged or staged. Click it to stage or unstage, or right-click the file. Stage All and Unstage All sit in the panel's header.

highlights.title: Time running.
highlights.body: While Claude works on a turn, the sidebar shows how long it has been going, next to the project and next to each branch.

summary: Tether 0.6.0 shows each branch's pull request and whether its checks passed.

highlights.title: Pull requests and checks.
highlights.body: A branch with a pull request shows its number next to the branch in the sidebar and on its Overview card, with a green check, a red cross or a clock for its checks. Hover for which checks failed, and click to open it on GitHub. A merged pull request marks its worktree as merged, squash merges included. This needs the GitHub CLI (gh), signed in.

summary: Tether 0.5.0 shows every Claude tab at a glance, in the window and in the menu bar.

highlights.title: Overview.
highlights.body: The Overview button at the top of the sidebar, or Command-0, shows a card for every Claude tab: what it's doing, what it wants permission for, its last message, lines changed and how long the turn has run. Click a card to open the tab.

highlights.title: Menu bar.
highlights.body: Tether's icon in the menu bar counts the tabs waiting on you. Its menu lists every Claude tab and what it's doing; pick one to jump to it. Turn it off in Settings > Appearance.

summary: Tether 0.4.0 shows two tabs side by side, lets you drag tabs into order, and can update itself from a release.

highlights.title: Split panes.
highlights.body: Command-D opens a shell beside the current tab, in the same folder. File > Split Down stacks it instead. Right-click any tab and choose Show Beside Current Tab to pair two you already have. Drag the divider to resize, double-click it to even it out, and use Command-[ and Command-] to move between the halves.

highlights.title: Drag tabs.
highlights.body: Drag a tab left or right onto another to move it there; the order is kept when Tether restarts. Drag a tab down onto the terminal to show it beside the one you are on.

highlights.title: Updates.
highlights.body: A signed release build checks GitHub for new releases and installs them with Tether > Check for Updates. Builds you make with make dev still update with git pull.

summary: Tether 0.3.0 reworks the Mac window around a chat view, a file browser and one-click shortcuts.

highlights.title: Terminal or chat.
highlights.body: A toggle in the top bar swaps a Claude tab's terminal for a chat view of the same conversation, with a message box at the bottom. Shift-Command-M switches back and forth.

highlights.title: Changes and Files.
highlights.body: The right panel is now Changes and Files. Files shows the project as a tree, without anything git ignores, with a filter. Click a file to read it over the terminal.

highlights.title: History.
highlights.body: History in the top bar lists this project's past Claude sessions with their titles, first prompts and branches. Search them, and open one to pick the conversation back up in a new tab.

highlights.title: Shortcuts.
highlights.body: Add commands like npm run dev with + > Edit Shortcuts. Each gets a button in the top bar and runs in its own tab. Click it again to jump back to the running one.

summary: Tether 0.2.0 puts your Claude sessions on your iPhone and gives the Mac app its own look.

highlights.title: Your iPhone, connected.
highlights.body: Pair the iPhone app with a QR code in Settings > iPhone. It connects over Tailscale, lists every project and thread, mirrors the conversation live, and lets you message Claude and answer permission prompts.

highlights.title: Notifications and Live Activities.
highlights.body: Lock-screen alerts when Claude needs permission, asks a question or finishes, with Allow, Deny and Reply buttons that work without opening the app. A Live Activity follows each running thread. Add your Apple push key in Settings > iPhone > Notifications.

highlights.title: Start work from your phone.
highlights.body: Start a task in any project, optionally on a new branch with its own worktree, in the permission mode you pick. Worktrees nest under their project in the sidebar and can be removed once merged.

highlights.title: One look.
highlights.body: The whole window follows your Ghostty theme, with letter tiles, pill tabs and a rounded terminal card. Settings > Appearance switches back to the system look.

highlights.title: Project icons.
highlights.body: If a project has an app icon, Tether shows it in the sidebar. It looks for .tether/icon.png, then an Xcode AppIcon, then a favicon or logo.

highlights.title: Move faster.
highlights.body: Command-1 to 9 switch projects, Command-T opens a Claude tab, Command-W closes one, and double-clicking a project name renames it.

summary: Tether 0.1.0 is a terminal workspace with a Claude session ready in every project.

highlights.title: A Claude session in every project.
highlights.body: Each project opens with Claude Code running, built on libghostty so your Ghostty theme and font carry over. Add shells and SSH tabs next to it.

highlights.title: Know what Claude is doing.
highlights.body: The sidebar shows sparkles while Claude works, a blue dot when it needs you and a green check when it's done.

highlights.title: Chat view.
highlights.body: Read any Claude tab as a conversation, with tool steps collapsed, and send messages without touching the terminal.

highlights.title: Changes against origin.
highlights.body: See what changed since the branch left main, open a diff, select lines and tell Claude what to change.
